In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms which regulate early embryonic gene expression in the sea urchin.
the molecular biology of sea urchin development.
the mechanisms of RNA metabolism in the early embryo of the sea urchin Lytechinus pictas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cytoplasmic postfertilization polyadenylation in the sea urchin egg and zygote is associated with the formation of a poly(A) protein (PAP) complex which may be involved in the subsequent activities of maternal messenger RNA.
poly(A) protein is involved in the control of mRNA activity during early development.
poly(A) sequences are not involved in the regulation of maternal mRNA translation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polyadenylated RNA's in the egg are not all the same and that the poly(A) sequences of the RNA's are not all in the same location.
the polyadenylated mRNAs are associated with proteins that are involved in the translation of maternal mRNAs during early development.

the polyadenylation of maternal mRNA's during the early stages of development is accompanied by a quantitative change in the number of protein-associated polyadenylate sequences, but not by the appearance of any novel poly(A)-associated protein species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an increased association of proteins with polyadenylated RNAs in sea urchins after fertilization.
there is an increase in the amount of poly(A) associated proteins in the early stages of development.
the poly(A) tail of the maternal mRNA in sea urchins is not only elongated after fertilization, but the poly(A) tails are also associated with specific proteins.
